input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: Response.__init__ reads self.raw.reason to initialize reason, but raw has no underlying response object yet at construction time, so the attribute access dereferences None.
- failure path: Any call that builds a Response, such as every adapter.send or a plain Response(), raises AttributeError ('NoneType' object has no attribute 'reason') before the object is populated, so no request can complete.

Reviewer finding
- description: Response.__init__ now assigns self.reason from self.raw.reason, but self.raw is initialized to None in the same constructor, so this attribute access fails.
- rationale: Trigger: any Response() construction, such as the one in adapters.build_response or a direct Response() in user or test code. Mechanism: in __init__ self.raw is still None when line 793 runs, so self.raw.reason raises AttributeError. Impact: every Response object creation crashes, breaking all requests calls and direct Response instantiation.
critique: Both describe the same defect: Response.__init__ reads self.raw.reason while raw is still None. That access raises AttributeError on every Response construction, which breaks all requests. The label's phrase "raw has no underlying response object" differs slightly from the finding's "self.raw is None", but both point to the same None dereference.
